name: Airships
what_failed: Rigid airships were the dominant long-distance air transport until Hindenburg disaster and airplane advancement made them obsolete.
why_it_failed: Airplanes became faster, cheaper, more reliable
Slow speed relative to emerging alternatives
assumptions_that_broke: Hydrogen could be made safe enough
Speed was less important than capacity
constraints_that_moved: Airplane speed and range improved exponentially
resurrection_conditions: Hybrid airship designs (Lockheed LMH-1, LTA Research)
lesson: A technology killed by a single catastrophic event can be resurrected when the original constraints change and the use case shifts. Airships failed as passenger transport but may succeed as heavy cargo. The cemetery is not permanent.
